reviewed_interpretation: Fresh I024 public-development evidence is valid and shipping-mirror exact. The disagreement population contains 16,297 frames (7,578 oracle-speech, 8,719 oracle-noise). No preregistered existing shipping observable provides strong and stable univariate speech/noise separation across domains. ratio_db has the highest global separability AUC at 0.6905, but its seven-noise-domain floor falls to 0.5854. shipping_probability has the strongest domain floor at 0.6247 but only 0.6607 global AUC and a 0.5857 SNR floor. upstream_margin is 0.6441 global with a 0.6048 domain floor; its three-frame mean reaches 0.6557 global but drops to a 0.5689 domain floor and 0.5469 SNR floor. The remaining preregistered numeric features are weaker, and noise_update_kind has only 0.0290 total-variation distance between speech and noise. Simple three-frame causal context therefore does not resolve the disagreement. I024 selects no feature, threshold or model. The repeated state-only guard/hold/observable route is closed under the preregistered observables; next root-cause work should move upstream to explain why NS speech_probability is high on the large disagreement-noise population, while respecting prior I014 evidence that upstream component synergy is useful in nonstationary conditions overall.

cross_slice_review.reviewed_interpretation: The feature ordering is not stable enough to support a state-only rule. ratio_db is strongest globally and becomes highly separable at high SNR, but degrades sharply in cafeteria noise. shipping_probability has the best domain floor but weakens at low SNR. Three-frame upstream/local summaries do not remove the domain/SNR sensitivity. The evidence is therefore consistent with condition-dependent overlap rather than a robust single shipping observable.

proposed_followup_hypothesis.rationale: I023 shows upstream-high/local-low disagreement is common on noise, and I024 finds no preregistered state-only observable with robust cross-domain univariate separation. Move the root-cause boundary upstream: on new fresh public-development authority, decompose NS speech_probability on oracle-noise disagreement frames into already-available upstream component/state diagnostics and short causal persistence, explicitly reconciling the result with I014's finding that upstream component synergy is useful on nonstationary speech/noise overall. The goal is causal localization, not reweighting, mapping or threshold selection.

verification_limits: I024 is candidate-zero and uses development-only oracle labels. ROC-AUC values describe the constructed public-development sampling distribution and are not calibrated product-environment error rates.

I024 evaluates preregistered univariate observables and simple causal three-frame summaries only. It does not establish that every possible multivariate classifier is incapable of separating disagreement speech and noise.
No numeric AUC, category distance or cross-slice statistic is a selected feature, threshold, model or shipping rule.

The closure ends further hand-designed state-only guard/hold/feature iteration under the tested observables; it does not invalidate prior I014 evidence that upstream component synergy can be useful in nonstationary regimes.
The artifact contains aggregate per-case/per-slice evidence but no raw audio archive.
